column7: UserGRPCService.projectCounts handled a RETURNED error from core.ProjectMembershipCounts but not a panic from the same call. userToProto calls it to build the RESPONSE for an already-created user, so a panic inside CountProjectMembershipsByUsers propagated past the committed User/UserRole/PasswordHistory/AuditEvent rows and RecoveryInterceptor turned it into Unavailable -- the caller saw an error for a request that had genuinely succeeded, with no returned ID to recover the user by. FuzzStorageFaultOperations found it on #2434 (oracle (a), differing tables [AuditEvent PasswordHistory User UserRole]). Fixed in #2408: projectCounts runs under besteffort.Run, so a panic yields absent (zero) counts rather than taking down the RPC; every userToProto caller (CreateUser, UpdateUser, GetUser, ListUsers) reaches it after its own primary write already committed, so the fix covers all four. Two independent non-vacuity checks, both run by FIX-2 against the pre-#2408 shape (besteffort.Run replaced by a direct call with only the returned error handled): the named proving test goes red, and the committed fuzz seed testdata/fuzz/FuzzStorageFaultOperations/5900200031 reproduces the issue's exact signature. That seed is index-addressed AND hash-named, so FIX-2 also registered it in seed_v2_test.go's seedIntent table -- without an entry it could silently re-point to another op/method on any storage-layer PR and keep passing under this claim's name, and its filename gives a reader no way to notice.
